question:
Consider the following statements about the Simon Commission:

1. It was boycotted by the Congress because it had no Indian member.

2. Its chairman was Sir John Simon.

3. It arrived in India in 1928 when Lord Irwin was the Viceroy.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Indian Statutory Commission, with seven British MPs and no Indian, was boycotted by the Congress (साइमन कमीशन का बहिष्कार — कोई भारतीय सदस्य नहीं)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the commission was named after its chairman Sir John Simon; Clement Attlee, a later Labour Prime Minister, was one member.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: it landed at Bombay on 3 February 1928, when Lord Irwin was Viceroy, and met with hartal, black flags and 'Simon Go Back'.

 

• The commission was appointed early in 1927 because the Conservatives feared losing the 1929 election.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1919 Act itself laid down a review after ten years.

 

• Its report of 1930 opposed diarchy and became the basis of the Government of India Act 1935.

 

• The Birkenhead challenge to Indians to frame a constitution followed.

 

• Congress boycotted the commission at its 1927 Madras session under M.A. Ansari, while the Justice Party and some others cooperated.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Dropping statement 3 is wrong because Irwin was Viceroy from 1926 to 1931, which covers the period of arrival in 1928.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Leaving out the first statement is wrong, as the all-white composition was the central objection and the Congress resolved to boycott it at Madras in 1927.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 4): Excluding statement 2 is incorrect since the Indian Statutory Commission is universally called the Simon Commission after its chairman Sir John Simon.

question: The Nehru Report of 1928, the first attempt by Indians to draft a constitution, was prepared by a committee chaired by
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motilal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State, challenged Indians to produce a constitution acceptable to all, and an all-party meeting appointed a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru with Jawaharlal Nehru as Secretary (नेहरू रिपोर्ट 1928 — मोतीलाल नेहरू अध्यक्ष)

 

• The eight-member committee submitted its report on 28 August 1928; it was the first attempt by Indians to prepare a draft constitution.

 

• It demanded dominion status, joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities and a declaration of fundamental rights.

 

• Jinnah's amendments to the report were rejected at the Calcutta convention, hardening the League's stand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

 

• The Lahore session of 1929 declared Purna Swaraj, effectively rejecting dominion status as a goal.

 

• The Simon Commission's boycott had pushed Indians toward the all-party effort.

 

• Motilal Nehru's report was also notable because it rejected separate electorates, while granting reservation to minorities in some provinces.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 1): Jawaharlal Nehru acted as Secretary of the committee, not its chairman, and he was then only a general secretary of the Congress, so he cannot be given the chair.

 

• Tej Bahadur Sapru (Option 3): Tej Bahadur Sapru was a liberal member of the committee and contributed to the draft, but the chair rested with the Congress veteran, not the lawyer from Allahabad.

 

• M.A. Jinnah (Option 4): Jinnah did not join the committee; he objected to the report's rejection of separate electorates and reservations, and replied later with his Fourteen Points.

question: Vallabhbhai Patel was given the title 'Sardar' by the women of which movement of 1928?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bardoli Satyagraha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 in Gujarat, the women who joined the struggle gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title Sardar (बारडोली सत्याग्रह 1928 — पटेल को सरदार की उपाधि)

 

• Bardoli had been hit by floods and famine, yet the Bombay Presidency raised the land revenue by 22 per cent.

 

• In January 1928 the farmers asked Patel to lead them; Gandhi backed the cause through articles in Young India.

 

• A commission under Maxwell and Broomfield inquired and the increase was cut to 6.03 per cent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bardoli drew national attention and money flowed in from many provinces.

 

• Kunverji Mehta and Jugatram Dave were among local leaders.

 

• Patel had also led the Kheda movement in 1918.

 

• Bardoli was also the site where the Congress Working Committee met in February 1922 to suspend Non-Cooperation.

 

• The Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry confirmed that the revenue enhancement was unjustified, a victory that made Patel a national figure.

 

NOTE

 

• Kheda Satyagraha (Option 1): Kheda was Patel's earlier campaign of 1918 against revenue collection after crop failure, and the Sardar title came a decade afterwards from a different movement.

 

• Champaran Satyagraha (Option 2): Champaran was the Bihar indigo struggle of 1917 led by Gandhi himself, in which Patel played no leading role, so the title could not have originated there.

 

• Dharasana Satyagraha (Option 4): Dharasana was the 1930 salt works raid led by Sarojini Naidu and Imam Sahib after Gandhi's arrest, a part of the Civil Disobedience Movement and not the origin of the Sardar title.

question: The Lahore session of the Congress in December 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. Which of the following was decided at this session?
option_2: Fundamental Rights were adopted as part of the Congress resolution
option_4: The goal of Purna Swaraj was declared and 26 January 1930 was fixed as Independence Day
solution_text:
The correct answer is The goal of Purna Swaraj was declared and 26 January 1930 was fixed as Independence Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Lahore session, held on the bank of the Ravi under Jawaharlal Nehru, Purna Swaraj (complete independence) was declared the goal of the Congress (लाहौर अधिवेशन 1929 — पूर्ण स्वराज)

 

• 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Purna Swatantrata Diwas, and the tricolour was hoisted across the country.

 

• The session also authorised the Congress Working Committee to launch a programme of civil disobedience.

 

• The Fundamental Rights resolution came later, at Karachi in 1931.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Congress ultimatum to the government for dominion status expired at the end of 1929.

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar set up the All India Depressed Classes Association on 8 August 1930.

 

• 26 January was chosen later as the date on which the Constitution came into force in 1950.

 

• The Lahore session was held during the days of Lord Irwin's declaration of October 1929 on dominion status as the goal.

 

NOTE

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement was approved (Option 1): The Non-Cooperation Movement was approved in 1920 at Calcutta and Nagpur, nine years before the Lahore session, so it cannot be the decision of 1929.

 

• Fundamental Rights were adopted as part of the Congress resolution (Option 2): Fundamental Rights were first discussed at the Karachi session of 1931 presided over by Sardar Patel, not at Lahore in 1929.

 

• The Poona Pact was endorsed (Option 3): The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar, years after the Lahore session, hence it could not have been endorsed in 1929.

question: The Salt Act, which gave the British a monopoly over production and taxation of salt and was violated by Gandhi at Dandi, was passed in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1882.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Salt Act of 1882 gave the colonial government a monopoly over the manufacture and sale of salt, and made making salt from seawater a criminal offence (नमक कानून 1882 — दांडी यात्रा का कारण)

 

• Until then Indians had been free to make salt from seawater without paying any charge.

 

• Gandhi selected the salt law as the focus of the Civil Disobedience Movement because salt was a daily necessity affecting rich and poor alike.

 

• On the morning of 6 April 1930 he broke the law at Dandi by making salt from seawater.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi first sent an eleven-point ultimatum to the Viceroy, and the deadline expired on 31 January 1930.

 

• The tax on salt was one of the demands among the eleven points.

 

• Sarojini Naidu, Imam Sahib and Manilal Gandhi continued the salt raids after his arrest.

 

• After the Dandi event, thousands of Indians, including women, made salt in coastal towns and courted arrest.

 

NOTE

 

• 1857 (Option 1): The year 1857 is the Great Revolt, long before the salt monopoly law; no salt legislation of that year is associated with Gandhi's march.

 

• 1905 (Option 3): The year 1905 marks the partition of Bengal, a different grievance that led to Swadeshi and Boycott, and it has no link with the salt tax.

 

• 1919 (Option 4): The year 1919 belongs to the Rowlatt Act and the Government of India Act, so it is far from the 1882 enactment targeted at Dandi.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Dandi March:

1. It started from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers.

2. Gandhi broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

3. It was launched against the Salt Act passed in 1930.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the march began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 volunteers and covered roughly 385 km to Dandi (दांडी यात्रा 12 मार्च 1930 — 78 साथी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Gandhi reached Dandi on 5 April and on the morning of 6 April 1930 broke the law by making salt.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the monopoly law was the Salt Act of 1882, not an Act of 1930; Gandhi protested against an old Act.

 

• The march began the Civil Disobedience Movement, which spread across the country and drew the attention of the world press.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi urged people to resign from jobs and legislatures.

 

• He said students would not attend school and the law would be disobeyed in every way.

 

• In the south, C. Rajagopalachari led a parallel march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam.

 

• Gandhi was arrested on 5 May 1930 at Karadi, and the salt raid at Dharasana was led by Sarojini Naidu.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Dropping the opening statement is wrong since the date of departure and the figure of 78 followers are standard and not in dispute.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Combining the second and third statements accepts the incorrect year of the Act, and also removes the correct starting date, so this pair is unacceptable.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Selecting every statement ignores that the Salt Act dates back to 1882, and Gandhi in 1930 only disobeyed it; the third statement is therefore false.

question: Gandhi attended the Round Table Conference in London as the sole representative of the Congress at which session?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Second Round Table Conference (1931).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference, held in London from 7 September 1931, as the Congress representative (दूसरा गोलमेज सम्मेलन 1931 — गांधी की भागीदारी)

 

• Other participants included Sarojini Naidu, B.R. Ambedkar, Annie Besant, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

 

• Jinnah and Ambedkar demanded separate electorates, which Gandhi firmly opposed, and the conference failed on the communal question.

 

• Gandhi returned disappointed, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was resumed in January 1932.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first conference (12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931) was held without the Congress as its leaders were in jail.

 

• The third conference had only 48 members from India.

 

• Its proposals led to the White Paper of 1933 and the Government of India Act of 1935.

 

• The Communal Award announced by Ramsay MacDonald in August 1932 followed this conference's failure on communal issues.

 

NOTE

 

• First Round Table Conference (1930) (Option 2): The first conference was held when Congress leaders were in prison after the Dandi campaign, and the party did not take part, so Gandhi could not have been there.

 

• Third Round Table Conference (1932) (Option 3): The third conference had no Congress invitation either; its leaders were in jail, and few results emerged beyond a White Paper in 1933.

 

• Simla Conference (1945) (Option 4): The Simla Conference of 1945 was convened under Viceroy Wavell within India, not at London, and it came fourteen years after the Round Table talks.

question: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
option_1: Withdrawal of ordinances curtailing Congress activities
option_2: Release of political prisoners not guilty of violence
option_3: Immediate grant of Purna Swaraj to India
option_4: Permission to coastal people to make salt for their own use
solution_text:
The correct answer is Immediate grant of Purna Swaraj to India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact) of 1931 did not promise independence, and granting Purna Swaraj was not part of it (गांधी-इरविन समझौता 1931 — पूर्ण स्वराज का वादा नहीं)

 

• Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference.

 

• In return all ordinances restricting Congress were to be withdrawn, and political prisoners not convicted of violence released.

 

• People living on the coast were allowed to produce salt for their own consumption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pact was signed in March 1931 after talks between Gandhi and Viceroy Irwin.

 

• In January 1931 the government lifted the ban on the Congress and released Gandhi and other leaders to create goodwill.

 

• Younger leaders like Nehru and Bose were unhappy over the pact.

 

• The pact is known as a truce because Gandhi was treated as an equal by the Viceroy, which angered Churchill who referred to a half-naked fakir.

 

NOTE

 

• Withdrawal of ordinances curtailing Congress activities (Option 1): Withdrawal of the repressive ordinances against the Congress was one of the concessions the government made to restore normal conditions, so it forms part of the terms.

 

• Release of political prisoners not guilty of violence (Option 2): Release of prisoners who had not been guilty of violence was agreed under the Delhi settlement, though those convicted of violent crimes remained in jail.

 

• Permission to coastal people to make salt for their own use (Option 4): Allowing coastal residents to make salt for personal use was a genuine concession, though it did not repeal the Salt Act or permit commercial manufacture.

question: The Karachi session of the Congress in 1931, presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is remembered for
option_2: the split between Moderates and Extremists
option_3: the approval of the Poona Pact
option_4: the first discussion of Fundamental Rights
solution_text:
The correct answer is the first discussion of Fundamental Rights.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At Karachi in 1931, with Vallabhbhai Patel as president, the Congress adopted a resolution on Fundamental Rights and a basic economic programme (कराची अधिवेशन 1931 — मौलिक अधिकारों पर पहली चर्चा)

 

• The session endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and authorised Gandhi to represent the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference.

 

• Gandhi said the party would continue on the non-violent path while Bhagat Singh was hanged just days before the session.

 

• Black flag demonstrations met Gandhi because of the executions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Rights resolution influenced the framing of the Constitution of India.

 

• Purna Swaraj was declared at Lahore in 1929.

 

• The 1907 Surat session saw the split between Moderates and Extremists.

 

• The Karachi resolution also promised free primary education, minimum wages and the abolition of untouchability.

 

• Gandhi's remark at Karachi that he would continue on his non-violent path came days after the execution of Bhagat Singh and his comrades.

 

NOTE

 

• the declaration of Purna Swaraj (Option 1): Purna Swaraj was declared two years earlier at Lahore under Jawaharlal Nehru, so it is not the characteristic outcome of Karachi.

 

• the split between Moderates and Extremists (Option 2): The Surat split of 1907 between Moderates and Extremists belongs to the earlier phase of the national movement, long before Gandhi's leadership.

 

• the approval of the Poona Pact (Option 3): The Poona Pact of September 1932 followed the Karachi session by about a year and was signed between Gandhi and Ambedkar, not approved at the 1931 session.

question: The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 was an agreement on reservation of seats for the depressed classes. It was reached between
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Poona Pact (24 September 1932) was an agreement between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar, signed by Ambedkar for the Dalits, by Madan Mohan Malaviya for the Hindus and by Gandhi (पूना समझौता 1932 — गांधी और अंबेडकर)

 

• It ended Gandhi's fast in Yerwada jail, undertaken against the Communal Award, which had given separate electorates to the depressed classes.

 

• Instead of separate electorates, seats were reserved for the depressed classes within the general (joint) electorate.

 

• The number of reserved seats was raised compared with the Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Communal Award was announced by Ramsay MacDonald in August 1932.

 

• Ambedkar had established the All India Depressed Classes Association in 1930.

 

• Gandhi later founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

 

• Gandhi began the fast on 20 September 1932 in Yerwada jail, and ended it on 26 September after the agreement.

 

• Ambedkar had agreed to give up separate electorates in exchange for 148 reserved seats, nearly double the number in the Communal Award.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandhi and Lord Irwin (Option 1): Gandhi and Irwin concluded the Delhi Pact in March 1931 on the suspension of Civil Disobedience, which is a separate agreement with a different subject.

 

• Nehru and Jinnah (Option 2): Nehru and Jinnah never signed a pact on the depressed classes; Jinnah's concern in this period was the Muslim share in legislatures.

 

• Ambedkar and Ramsay MacDonald (Option 4): Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award which the pact modified; he was the British Prime Minister and not a signatory to the Poona agreement.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:

1. It was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament for India up to that time.

2. Burma was separated from India under it in 1937.

3. It introduced diarchy in the provinces for the first time.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Government of India Act 1935 was the lengthiest Act enacted by the British Parliament for India (भारत शासन अधिनियम 1935 — सबसे लंबा अधिनियम)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Burma was separated from British India in 1937 under this Act.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: diarchy in the provinces was introduced by the 1919 Act; the 1935 Act abolished it in the provinces and gave provincial autonomy.

 

• Its provisions drew on the White Paper of 1933 that emerged from the Round Table Conferences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Federation, provincial autonomy and bicameral legislatures in some provinces were features of the Act.

 

• Elections under it were held in 1937 and the Congress formed ministries in most provinces.

 

• The Simon Commission recommended autonomous government instead of diarchy.

 

• Provincial elections under the Act were held in 1937, and Congress won an absolute majority in five provinces.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Choosing the second and third statements accepts the false claim about diarchy while leaving out the correct claim on the Act's length, so it is unsound.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): The first and third statements pair a correct fact with the false suggestion that the 1935 Act began diarchy, which actually dates to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Picking all three ignores that diarchy was the 1919 innovation; the 1935 Act did away with it in the provinces and tried to place it at the Centre instead.

question: Arrange the following events of the Second World War period in chronological order.
option_1: Lahore Resolution – Resignation of Congress ministries – August Offer – Cripps Mission
option_2: Resignation of Congress ministries – August Offer – Lahore Resolution – Cripps Mission
option_3: Resignation of Congress ministries – Lahore Resolution – August Offer – Cripps Mission
option_4: Resignation of Congress ministries – Lahore Resolution – Cripps Mission – August Offer
solution_text:
The correct answer is Resignation of Congress ministries – Lahore Resolution – August Offer – Cripps Mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939, protesting at India being dragged into the war without consultation (क्रम: 1939 इस्तीफे, मार्च 1940 लाहौर प्रस्ताव, अगस्त 1940 प्रस्ताव, 1942 क्रिप्स)

 

• The Muslim League's Lahore Resolution demanding Pakistan was passed in March 1940.

 

• The August Offer of Viceroy Linlithgow came on 8 August 1940.

 

• The Cripps Mission arrived in March 1942, after the failure of the August proposals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• World War II began on 1 September 1939.

 

• Gandhi launched the Individual Satyagraha in October 1940.

 

• The Quit India resolution followed the failure of Cripps in August 1942.

 

• The Congress ministries had come to power in July 1937 in seven provinces after the first elections under the 1935 Act.

 

• The Second World War ended in 1945, and its end brought a Labour government to power in Britain under Attlee.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore Resolution – Resignation of Congress ministries – August Offer – Cripps Mission (Option 1): This sequence places the League's Lahore Resolution before the Congress ministries' resignation, though the ministries quit in late 1939 and the resolution came in March 1940.

 

• Resignation of Congress ministries – August Offer – Lahore Resolution – Cripps Mission (Option 2): Here the August Offer precedes the Lahore Resolution; in fact the League's demand of March 1940 came five months before Linlithgow's offer of August.

 

• Resignation of Congress ministries – Lahore Resolution – Cripps Mission – August Offer (Option 4): The order shown puts the Cripps Mission ahead of the August Offer, but the Cripps proposals of 1942 were made after the failure of the 1940 offer.

question: The August Offer of 8 August 1940, announced by Viceroy Linlithgow, for the first time
option_1: acknowledged the right of Indians to frame their own constitution
option_4: announced the transfer of power by June 1948
solution_text:
The correct answer is acknowledged the right of Indians to frame their own constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The August Offer of 8 August 1940 acknowledged, for the first time, the right of Indians to frame their own constitution after the war (अगस्त प्रस्ताव 1940 — संविधान निर्माण का अधिकार)

 

• It proposed that after the war a representative body of Indians would frame the new constitution, with Dominion status as the objective.

 

• The Viceroy's Executive Council was to have more Indians than Britons.

 

• The Congress rejected it, with Nehru calling Dominion status 'dead as a doornail', and the Muslim League wanted nothing short of partition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The offer was made when Britain feared a Nazi invasion and wanted Congress support for the war.

 

• Gandhi then launched the Individual Satyagraha, with Vinoba Bhave as the first Satyagrahi.

 

• Attlee announced the June 1948 deadline in February 1947.

 

• The Congress had demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise before the August Offer was announced.

 

NOTE

 

• granted Purna Swaraj to India (Option 2): Complete independence was the Congress demand, not what the offer conceded; the offer talked only of Dominion status after the war and so fell short.

 

• promised partition of the country (Option 3): Partition was never promised in the August Offer; the League wanted it, but the document merely said minorities' views should be respected.

 

• announced the transfer of power by June 1948 (Option 4): The June 1948 deadline came in Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947, almost seven years after Linlithgow's offer.

question: Who was the first Satyagrahi chosen by Gandhi in the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinoba Bhave.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi launched the Individual Satyagraha after the August Offer, choosing the Satyagrahis himself, and Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first to offer it (व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह 1940 — विनोबा भावे पहले सत्याग्रही)

 

• The campaign was limited, symbolic and strictly non-violent; each Satyagrahi made anti-war speeches and courted arrest.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru was the second Satyagrahi and Braham Dutt the third.

 

• It lasted for about fifteen months, and was also accompanied by the 'Delhi Chalo' march of the Satyagrahis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vinoba Bhave got three months' imprisonment and Nehru four.

 

• Bhave later led the Bhoodan movement from 1951.

 

• The Individual Satyagraha was followed by the Cripps Mission.

 

• Gandhi's choice of Vinoba showed his stress on constructive work, for Vinoba lived in the Paunar ashram near Wardha.

 

• The Individual Satyagraha was not meant to embarrass Britain militarily, since Gandhi wanted to protest war participation without hampering the war effort itself.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 1): Jawaharlal Nehru offered Satyagraha second, and was jailed for four months, so he was not the one who opened the campaign.

 

• Braham Dutt (Option 2): Braham Dutt was the third person chosen by Gandhi and is far less known, but he did not begin the movement.

 

• Sardar Patel (Option 3): Sardar Patel was not selected among the first Satyagrahis and was kept for guiding the party; he was arrested later in 1942 with other leaders.

question: Gandhi described the proposals brought by the Cripps Mission in 1942 as
option_1: a bundle of empty promises on a sinking ship
option_2: a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank
option_3: a golden cage for the Indian people
option_4: a compromise on the edge of a sword
solution_text:
The correct answer is a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhi called the Cripps offer 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank', since Dominion status would be given only after the war while Britain's fortunes seemed to be failing (क्रिप्स प्रस्ताव पर गांधी की टिप्पणी, 1942)

 

• The Cripps Mission promised Dominion status after the war, protection of minorities and a Constituent Assembly with representatives of British provinces and Princely States.

 

• It was sent after the failure of the August Offer and amid the Japanese advance in Asia.

 

• The Congress rejected it because of the post-war timing and the provision allowing provinces to stay out, while the Muslim League was dissatisfied because Pakistan was not conceded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the War Cabinet and leader of the House of Commons.

 

• Failure of the mission led directly to the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

 

• Cripps was later part of the 1946 Cabinet Mission as President of the Board of Trade.

 

• Cripps proposed that provinces unwilling to join the Union could frame separate constitutions, which alarmed the Congress.

 

NOTE

 

• a bundle of empty promises on a sinking ship (Option 1): This phrase about a sinking ship is invented and was not used by Gandhi about the Cripps proposals; the known remark involved a post-dated cheque and a bank.

 

• a golden cage for the Indian people (Option 3): The golden cage expression was never applied to the Cripps proposals by Gandhi, and it does not appear in the record of his reaction to the Mission.

 

• a compromise on the edge of a sword (Option 4): The sword-edge compromise wording has no basis in his comments on the Cripps offer, which he rejected in banking terms instead.

question:
Assertion (A): The Quit India Movement of 1942 was largely leaderless and spontaneous.

Reason (R): Almost all prominent Congress leaders were arrested on 8-9 August 1942 under Operation Zero Hour.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: with the top leaders in jail the movement was carried on by the people in a spontaneous manner (भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन 1942 — नेतृत्वविहीन)

 

• Reason R is true: on 8 August 1942 the AICC passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, and in the early hours the government arrested the leaders in Operation Zero Hour.

 

• Gandhi was kept at Poona, and Nehru, Azad and others at Ahmednagar Fort.

 

• Leadership then came from Ram Manohar Lohia, Achyut Patwardhan, S.M. Joshi and Jayaprakash Narayan, who worked underground.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on 8 August 1942.

 

• British repression included 538 rounds of firing, and about 60,000 persons were jailed.

 

• Gandhi was released in 1944 from the Aga Khan Palace after his health deteriorated.

 

• Gandhi's address in Hindustani ended with the words 'Do or Die' and he told people to consider themselves free.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): Claiming R does not explain A is wrong, because the removal of the leadership overnight is exactly why the agitation lost central direction and became popular and uncoordinated.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Saying A is true and R false is incorrect, as the arrests of 8-9 August under Operation Zero Hour are a documented event of the movement's first day.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): Declaring A false is incorrect since the absence of the arrested leaders is the standard description of the movement, with underground figures filling the gap.

question: Which of the following leaders did NOT support the Quit India Movement of 1942?
solution_text:
The correct answer is B.R. Ambedkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• B.R. Ambedkar, along with Tej Bahadur Sapru and the Hindu Mahasabha, did not support the Quit India Movement (भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन के विरोधी — अंबेडकर, सप्रू, हिंदू महासभा)

 

• Lohia, Achyut Patwardhan and S.M. Joshi gave leadership to the movement once the main leaders were jailed.

 

• Jayaprakash Narayan escaped from Hazaribagh jail and played an important role in the underground resistance.

 

• Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the national flag at Gowalia Tank on 9 August 1942 after the arrests.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Muslim League also kept away, asking for 'Divide and Quit'.

 

• The movement is also called August Kranti.

 

• Gowalia Tank Maidan is now known as August Kranti Maidan.

 

• Ambedkar was in the Viceroy's Executive Council as Labour Member in 1942, which explains his stand against the movement.

 

• The Hindu Mahasabha under V.D. Savarkar wanted Hindus to remain in the army, and Sapru also favoured cooperation with the Viceroy.

 

NOTE

 

• Ram Manohar Lohia (Option 2): Ram Manohar Lohia was an active underground leader who ran the Congress Radio in Bombay, so he plainly supported the movement and is not the exception.

 

• Jayaprakash Narayan (Option 3): Jayaprakash Narayan took a prominent role, organising an underground network after escaping from jail, hence he cannot be the person who stayed away.

 

• Aruna Asaf Ali (Option 4): Aruna Asaf Ali raised the flag at Gowalia Tank and went underground, which makes her a well-known supporter rather than an opponent.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Army (INA):

1. Subhas Chandra Bose reached Singapore on 2 July 1943 and gave the call 'Dilli Chalo'.

2. The women's regiment of the INA was named after Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi.

3. The INA had a brigade named after Jawaharlal Nehru.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Bose reached Singapore on 2 July 1943, became head of the Indian Independence League and supreme commander of the INA, and gave the war cry 'Dilli Chalo' (आज़ाद हिंद फौज — बोस 2 जुलाई 1943 सिंगापुर)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the women's unit was the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: the INA's brigades were the Subhas Brigade, Gandhi Brigade and Nehru Brigade.

 

• Bose's slogan 'Jai Hind' was adopted by the soldiers, who called him Netaji.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bose is believed to have died on 18 August 1945 in a plane crash in Taiwan.

 

• The INA advanced towards Imphal and Kohima in 1944 with Japanese support.

 

• Prakram Diwas is observed on 23 January, his birth anniversary, since 2021.

 

• The INA trials at the Red Fort in 1945-46 against Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal and Gurbaksh Dhillon roused the nation.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Leaving out the Nehru Brigade is wrong since the INA included brigades named after Gandhi and Nehru as well as Subhas.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Omitting the first statement is incorrect: Bose's arrival at Singapore in July 1943, from where he gave 'Dilli Chalo', is the central date of the INA's second phase.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 4): Excluding the women's regiment is wrong because the Rani of Jhansi Regiment under Captain Lakshmi Sahgal was a well-known unit of the Azad Hind Fauj.

question: The Shimla Conference of 1945, convened by Viceroy Wavell on the Wavell Plan, failed mainly because
option_1: Gandhi refused to attend the conference
option_3: the British withdrew the plan before the meeting
option_4: Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League could nominate Muslim members
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League could nominate Muslim members.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shimla Conference (1945) was convened to discuss the Wavell Plan for an Executive Council and Indian self-government; it failed as Jinnah insisted only the Muslim League could name the Muslim members (शिमला सम्मेलन 1945 — जिन्ना की जिद)

 

• The Congress, which claimed to represent all communities, opposed this demand and refused to accept nomination limited to the League.

 

• Because the two parties could not agree, it was seen as the last chance to avoid partition.

 

• After the war a Labour government was elected in Britain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The conference met in June-July 1945.

 

• Maulana Azad, the Congress president, led the Congress delegation.

 

• The failure strengthened the League's claim as the sole spokesman of Muslims.

 

• Lord Wavell, a soldier, was Viceroy from 1943 to 1947 and was replaced by Mountbatten.

 

• The Wavell Plan proposed an Executive Council in which the Viceroy and the Commander-in-Chief would be the only non-Indians, with parity between caste Hindus and Muslims.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandhi refused to attend the conference (Option 1): Gandhi did not hold a Congress post then, and the Congress was represented by Maulana Azad, so the failure cannot be attributed to his absence.

 

• the Congress demanded immediate Pakistan (Option 2): It was the League that wanted Pakistan; the Congress opposed that demand, so the Congress did not ask for it at Shimla.

 

• the British withdrew the plan before the meeting (Option 3): The British did not scrap the plan beforehand; the conference actually met and talks broke down over representation, not due to a withdrawal.

question: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clement Attlee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cabinet Mission of 1946 had three British Cabinet ministers: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander; Clement Attlee was the Prime Minister who sent it (कैबिनेट मिशन 1946 के सदस्य)

 

• Attlee announced on 15 March 1946 that India's right to self-determination and framing of a Constitution had been conceded.

 

• Pethick-Lawrence was Secretary of State for India, Cripps was President of the Board of Trade and Alexander was First Lord of the Admiralty.

 

• Its aim was to discuss the transfer of power from the British to Indian leadership.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Attlee had been a member of the Simon Commission in 1928.

 

• The Mission proposed a three-tier structure with groups of provinces.

 

• A Constituent Assembly was formed in December 1946.

 

• The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and its Plan was announced on 16 May 1946.

 

• The Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a full sovereign Pakistan, and proposed a three-group scheme within a loose union.

 

NOTE

 

• Pethick Lawrence (Option 2): Pethick-Lawrence, the Secretary of State for India, headed the Mission and is among its three members, so he cannot be the exception.

 

• Stafford Cripps (Option 3): Stafford Cripps, President of the Board of Trade, was the second member; he had visited India earlier in 1942 with a separate mission.

 

• A.V. Alexander (Option 4): A.V. Alexander, First Lord of the Admiralty, was the third member, which rules him out as the person who did not belong to the mission.

question: The Interim Government of India, with Jawaharlal Nehru as its head, was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan on
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 September 1946.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Interim Government under Jawaharlal Nehru was formed on 2 September 1946, after elections held in July 1946 (अंतरिम सरकार 2 सितंबर 1946 — नेहरू के नेतृत्व में)

 

• The Mission also envisaged an executive council supported by the major Indian parties and a Constituent Assembly for framing the Constitution.

 

• Congress governments were formed in most provinces including the NWFP, while the League ruled Bengal and Sindh.

 

• Jinnah withdrew acceptance of the plan and called Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constituent Assembly met for the first time in December 1946.

 

• Direct Action Day was followed by serious communal riots in Calcutta.

 

• The Muslim League later joined the Interim Government in October 1946.

 

• The League joined the Interim Government in October 1946 but did not attend the Constituent Assembly at first.

 

NOTE

 

• 16 August 1946 (Option 1): 16 August 1946 was the date of the League's Direct Action Day, which preceded the formation of the Interim Government by about two weeks; it is therefore a separate and earlier event.

 

• 15 August 1947 (Option 2): 15 August 1947 is the day India became independent, nearly a year after the Interim Government began functioning, so it cannot be the date asked for here.

 

• 9 December 1946 (Option 3): 9 December 1946 is the day the Constituent Assembly assembled for its first session, and is a separate event from the formation of the Interim Government.

question: In February 1947 Prime Minister Attlee announced the transfer of power to responsible Indian hands by a date not later than
solution_text:
The correct answer is June 1948.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 20 February 1947 Attlee announced that Britain would transfer power to responsible Indian hands by a date not later than June 1948 (अटली की घोषणा 20 फरवरी 1947 — जून 1948 तक सत्ता हस्तांतरण)

 

• He also decided to send Lord Mountbatten as the new Viceroy, in place of Wavell.

 

• Mountbatten took charge as Viceroy on 24 March 1947 and soon concluded that the date had to be advanced.

 

• The 3 June Plan fixed partition and power transfer for 15 August 1947.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and the first Governor-General of independent India.

 

• Wavell had been Viceroy since 1943.

 

• Jinnah celebrated Pakistan Day on 23 March 1947.

 

• Mountbatten advanced the date of independence from June 1948 to August 1947, choosing the second anniversary of Japan's surrender.

 

• The Radcliffe Award was announced only on 17 August 1947, two days after independence, which led to confusion and large-scale migration.

 

NOTE

 

• August 1947 (Option 1): August 1947 was the actual date of independence after the plan was hastened, but Attlee's February announcement named a deadline ten months later.

 

• January 1949 (Option 2): January 1949 is later than any date mentioned in the announcement; the British government did not extend the outer limit beyond mid-1948.

 

• December 1947 (Option 4): December 1947 was never given in the statement; the outer date announced was mid-1948, and independence arrived earlier than that.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Mountbatten (3 June) Plan:

1. It provided for partition into India and Pakistan effective 15 August 1947.

2. A Boundary Commission headed by Cyril Radcliffe was to demarcate the boundaries of Punjab and Bengal.

3. It was accepted by the Congress but rejected by the Muslim League.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the plan provided for partition into India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947, with a separate Constituent Assembly for Pakistan (माउंटबेटन योजना 3 जून 1947)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the Radcliffe Boundary Commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the borders of Punjab and Bengal.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the 3 June Plan was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

 

• The Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed on 18 July 1947 to implement it, and the assemblies of Bengal and Punjab voted on partition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Princely states were free to join India or Pakistan or even remain independent under the plan.

 

• The earlier Dickie Bird Plan of May 1947 was dubbed Plan Balkan by Nehru.

 

• Sardar Patel was the first leader to accept the inevitability of partition to stop violence.

 

• The Indian Independence Act 1947 ended the paramountcy of the Crown over the princely states from 15 August 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Pairing the second and third statements accepts the false claim that the League rejected the plan, and wrongly excludes the correct partition date.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Combining the first and third statements includes the untrue refusal by the League and leaves out the Radcliffe Commission, which is a firm provision.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Choosing all three overlooks that the League accepted the plan, since it conceded Pakistan; only the Congress was reluctant over partition.

question:
Match the milestones in the demand for Pakistan with the year.

Column A: (a) Mohammad Iqbal outlined a Muslim state (b) Choudhary Rahmat Ali used the word 'Pakistan' (c) Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League (d) 'Divide and Quit' slogan at Karachi session

Column B: (i) 1940 (ii) 1930 (iii) 1943 (iv) 1933
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iqbal presented the idea of a Muslim state in 1930; Rahmat Ali coined the word Pakistan in 1933; the Lahore Resolution came in 1940; the slogan 'Divide and Quit' was adopted in 1943 (पाकिस्तान की माँग के चरण — 1930, 1933, 1940, 1943)

 

• The Lahore session of the League in 1940 was presided over by M.A. Jinnah.

 

• The Karachi session of the League in 1943 adopted the slogan given by Jinnah.

 

• Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947 with Karachi as capital and Jinnah as Governor-General.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Iqbal's song 'Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindustan Hamara' is famous.

 

• Rahmat Ali's pamphlet 'Now or Never' of 1933 popularised the term.

 

• Jinnah celebrated Pakistan Day on 23 March 1947.

 

• The 1940 Lahore Resolution was moved by A.K. Fazlul Huq, the Bengal Prime Minister, and seconded by Khaliquzzaman.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 1): This key reverses Iqbal and Rahmat Ali's years, giving 1933 to Iqbal and 1930 to the person who coined the name, which contradicts the order of events.

 

• a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i (Option 3): Here the Lahore Resolution is given the year 1943 and the Karachi slogan 1940, but the Lahore session preceded the Karachi session by three years.

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii (Option 4): This option assigns 1940 to Iqbal, though Iqbal had spoken of a Muslim state at the 1930 Allahabad session, a decade before the Lahore Resolution.

question: Jatin Das, a revolutionary arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case, died in jail in 1929 after a hunger strike of how many days, demanding that political prisoners be treated as such?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 63 days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jatin Das went on hunger strike in Lahore jail demanding better treatment and the status of political prisoners, and died in September 1929 after 63 days (जतिन दास का 63 दिन का अनशन, 1929)

 

• He had been arrested after the Assembly bombing period along with other members of the HSRA.

 

• His death roused public sympathy and turned the attention of the whole country to the conditions inside prisons.

 

• Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt also fasted for the cause.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhagat Singh was arrested after the bombing of the Assembly on 8 April 1929.

 

• Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged on 23 March 1931.

 

• The HSRA had been reorganised by Azad in September 1928.

 

• Jatin Das's funeral procession in Calcutta in September 1929 was attended by huge crowds, led by Subhas Bose.

 

NOTE

 

• 21 days (Option 1): A fast of twenty-one days was a symbolic period used by Gandhi in 1933 and 1924, and it does not correspond to the Lahore jail strike.

 

• 45 days (Option 2): A forty-five day figure does not match the recorded length of the hunger strike which led to his death; the fast continued well beyond that.

 

• 78 days (Option 3): Seventy-eight is the count of Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March, which a candidate may confuse with the duration of the strike.
